function: Semantic speech-to-text transmission over SVD-precoded MIMO (learned codec and importance network) plus a CNN ChanEst network that refines a conventionally pre-estimated MIMO channel (p. 8).
system: SU-MIMO N=4 BS and M=4 user antennas (2x2 to 32x32 tested), MU-MIMO N=16, M=4, K=4; SVD precoding; no RIS; band not stated (p. 3, 10, 12).
method: Supervised: CNN-transformer semantic codec (CTC loss), dense semantic-aware network trained separately and fine-tuned for MU-MIMO; ChanEst 2D CNN with MSE loss, trained jointly with SAC-ST (p. 5-8).
data_channel: Simulated Rayleigh fading SU-MIMO and MU-MIMO channels; LibriSpeech 960h speech corpus for training and testing; no 3GPP or measured channel (p. 8-9).
test_conditions: Test SNR from -8 to 22 dB; SU-MIMO 4x4 plus other antenna and user counts; training SNR and per-configuration retraining not stated; MU-MIMO fine-tuned from SU-MIMO (p. 7-12).
baselines: Learned: DeepSC-ST [20] and Han's work [18] adapted to MIMO, DeepSC-ST 2.0 (without semantic-aware network); channel estimation: LS, MMSE, MMSE(joint), perfect CSI (p. 9-11).
metrics: Word error rate and sentence similarity versus SNR; trainable parameters (Table II); inference time (Table VI); equivalent subchannel SNR (Table IV) (p. 8, 10-12).
complexity: Trainable parameters: DeepSC-ST 2.0 9.12e7, semantic-aware network 3.17e3, ChanEst 2.11e5; inference time 0.039-0.047 s (SU-MIMO), 0.086-0.089 s (MU-MIMO) (p. 10, 12).
openness: GitHub link only for the equivalent-SNR data behind Table IV (github.com/Zhenzi-Weng/SAC-ST/tree/main/equivalent-SNR); no code statement; LibriSpeech is public (p. 9-10).
q1_support: p. 8: "SU-MIMO and MU-MIMO Rayleigh fading channels" are the only channels, from a custom simulator; the paper never mentions 3GPP, QuaDRiGa, DeepMIMO, or measured data.
q2_support: p. 7: "fine-tuned by minimising the overall CTC loss" is the only adaptation (SU-MIMO model fine-tuned for MU-MIMO) and its size is not reported; the antenna and user sweeps (Figs. 8, 11) never say a model trained for one setting is tested on another.
q3_support: p. 9: "the DeepSC-ST [20] and the system developed in [18] are considered as two benchmarks" (earlier learned systems, [20] by the same first author); p. 11: "with the conventional least square (LS) and minimum mean-square error (MMSE) channel estimation algorithms"; all compared on WER and sentence similarity.
q4_support: p. 9: "the trainable NN complexity of them is presented in Table II" (p. 10, parameters); p. 12: "the average model inference time of different systems under the SU-MIMO and MU-MIMO communication scenarios is provided in Table VI".
q5_support: p. 10: "is available at https://github.com/Zhenzi-Weng/SAC-ST/tree/main/equivalent-SNR" (footnote 1, the equivalent-SNR data behind Table IV); no code release is stated, and LibriSpeech is a public speech corpus of the learning task alone.
notes: Included as area 2 because the ChanEst network estimates the MIMO channel (p. 8); the semantic codec alone would fail the function check, so the reviewer should confirm. q3 mixes two experiments: earlier learned semantic systems [18], [20] (Fig. 7, p. 10) and LS/MMSE estimators (Fig. 9); no earlier learned channel estimator is compared. q2 is borderline (SU to MU fine-tuning, p. 7). q5 is borderline (only auxiliary data linked, p. 10).
